questions.stem: A 35-year-old man is found to have elevated alanine aminotransferase and aspartate aminotransferase levels. He has no abdominal pain, nausea, or vomiting. The patient has used intravenous drugs but denies significant alcohol use. His past medical history is negative for blood transfusions or excessive acetaminophen use. Physical examination findings are normal. Laboratory studies show high titers of IgG directed against the hepatitis C envelope protein. Which of the following is the most likely reason these antibodies do not confer effective immunity against the infection?

options.label: A
options.text: Envelope proteins are lost after recurrent viral replication

options.label: B
options.text: Envelope proteins are sequestered within hepatocytes

options.label: D
options.text: Envelope proteins have variations in their antigenic structure

questions.answerText: Envelope proteins have variations in their antigenic structure
questions.solutionHtml:
Envelope proteins have variations in their antigenic structure
  • Hepatitis C virus (HCV) has six or more genotypes and multiple subtypes that differ in genomic composition by as much as 30%-35%. This is mainly because the virion-encoded RNA-dependent RNA polymerase has no proofreading 3'-->5' exonuclease activity, resulting in many replication errors. Although most patients have a single genotype, the high mutation rate leads to distinct quasispecies within infected individuals over time.
  • These variant strains differ primarily at hypervariable genomic regions, such as those found in the sequences coding for its envelope glycoproteins. The continuous generation of novel envelope glycoproteins prevents infected individuals from mounting an effective immune response. As the production of host antibodies against a quasispecies commences, that strain dies off, and new ones occur. The tremendous antigenic variety of HCV has significantly slowed efforts to develop an effective vaccine.


Ananthanaryan and Paniker Textbook of Microbiology, 12th Edition, Page No. 233

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man comes to the emergency department after five days of progressive anorexia, nausea, and abdominal pain. The patient is a known hepatitis B carrier. He admits to using IV drugs and has shared needles with other drug users several times. His temperature is 37.7 C (99.9 F). Examination shows scleral icterus and mild, tender hepatomegaly. Laboratory studies are notable for highly elevated levels of liver aminotransferases and serum bilirubin and also offer the following results:Hepatitis B surface antigen +Hepatitis C virus antibody -HIV-1 antibody -Hepatitis D RNA +This patient's chronic infection assists which life cycle aspects of the current infectious agent?
questions.solutionHtml:
Coating of viral particles
  • Often referred to as the delta agent, hepatitis D virus (HDV) is a 35-nm, double-shelled particle that resembles the Dane particle of hepatitis B virus (HBV). The internal polypeptide assembly of HDV is designated hepatitis D antigen (HDAg). A very short, circular molecule of single-stranded RNA is associated with this antigen.
  • HDAg is considered replication defective as it must be coated by the outer coat hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) of HBV to penetrate the hepatocyte.
  • HDV infection can arise either as an acute coinfection with HBV or as a superinfection of a chronic HBV carrier.


Ananthanaryan and Paniker Textbook of Microbiology, 12th Edition, Page No. 324

questions.stem: An individual who has received all three doses of the hepatitis B vaccine and who has never had hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection would be expected to have which of the following serologic marker(s)?
questions.solutionHtml:
HBsAb

HBsAb is a rapid, self-performing, immunochromatographic assay for detecting HBsAb in human serum.



Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 732

questions.stem: WHICH of the following is true about the hepatitis C virus:

options.label: B
options.text: most typical indication for liver transplantation

options.label: D
options.text: Does not cause coinfection with hepatitis B

questions.answerText: most typical indication for liver transplantation
questions.solutionHtml:
most typical indication for liver transplantation

Hepatitis C is a liver disease caused by the hepatitis C virus (HCV); the virus can cause both acute and chronic hepatitis, ranging in severity from a mild illness lasting a few weeks to a serious, lifelong illness.



Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 673

questions.stem: To which of the viruses is hepatitis A most closely related genetically:
questions.solutionHtml:
Poliovirus

Hepatitis A virus (HAV), classified as hepatovirus, is a small, unenveloped symmetrical RNA virus that shares many of the characteristics of the picornavirus family and is the cause of infectious or epidemic hepatitis transmitted by the fecal-oral route.



Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 495

questions.stem: Acute Hepatitis A virus infection is best diagnosed by-
questions.solutionHtml:
IgM antibodies in serum
  • The HAV IgM antibody test detects the first antibody produced by the body when it is exposed to hepatitis A.
  • This test is used to detect early or recent infections and to diagnose the disease in people with symptoms of acute hepatitis.
  • It may be performed as part of an acute viral hepatitis panel.
  • This test looks for antibodies in your blood called IgM.
  • The test can determine whether you are infected with the hepatitis A virus (HAV).


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 495

questions.stem: In acute hepatitis B infection, which of the following is first to appear in serum:
questions.solutionHtml:
HbsAg

HBsAg (hepatitis B surface antigen) is the first serologic marker to appear in a new acute infection, which can be detected as early as one week and as late as nine weeks, with an average of one month after exposure to the hepatitis B virus (HBV).



Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 497

questions.stem: Marker of relative infectivity of serum in Hepatitis B is:
questions.solutionHtml:
HBe Ag

Hepatitis B e-antigen (HBeAg) is a small polypeptide that exists in an accessible form in the serum of individuals during the early phase of hepatitis B infection.



Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 497

questions.stem: A 33-year-old nurse suffered a needle stick injury. The patient used illicit intravenous drugs. One month later, the nurse developed jaundice. Which of the following findings would implicate hepatitis B as the etiology?
questions.solutionHtml:
Positive hepatitis B surface antigen
  • Hepatitis B infection is caused by the hepatitis B virus (HBV). The virus is passed from person to person through blood, semen, or other body fluids. It does not spread by sneezing or coughing.
  • Hepatitis B virus (HBV) is a Hepadnavirus, highly resistant to extremes of temperature and humidity, that invades the hepatocytes.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 497

questions.stem: Acute Hepatitis B infection is diagnosed by:
questions.solutionHtml:
Anti HBc IgM
  • Acute hepatitis B is a short-term illness that occurs within the first six months after someone is exposed to the hepatitis B virus.
  • Some people with acute hepatitis B have no symptoms or mild illness. For others, acute hepatitis B causes a more severe disease that requires hospitalization.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 498

questions.stem: A chronic infection of hepatitis B is defined as having demonstrated the presence of:

options.label: A
options.text: HBsAg for more than six months

options.label: B
options.text: Antibody against HBsAg for more than six months

options.label: C
options.text: Antibody against HBcAg for less than six months

options.label: D
options.text: HBcAg for more than six months

questions.answerText: HBsAg for more than six months
questions.solutionHtml:
HBsAg for more than six months
  • Hepatitis B infection becomes chronic, meaning it lasts more than six months.
  • Having chronic hepatitis B increases your risk of developing liver failure, liver cancer, or cirrhosis — a condition that permanently scars the liver.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 498

questions.stem: A hospital worker is found to have positive HbsAg & HbeAg. Which of the following best describes the worker?

options.label: A
options.text: Is infective and has active hepatitis

options.label: B
options.text: Is infective but does not have active hepatitis

options.label: D
options.text: Is evincing a biologic false-positive test for hepatitis

questions.answerText: Is infective and has active hepatitis
questions.solutionHtml:
Is infective and has active hepatitis

The association between hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and hepatitis B 'e' antigen (HBeAg) levels and liver inflammation and fibrosis in patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) in the immune clearance (IC) remains elusive.



Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 498

questions.stem: With regards to the newborn child of an HBV positive female, which is false:

options.label: D
options.text: Has a 90% chance of chronic infection if not treated ASAP.

questions.solutionHtml:
Should not be breastfed.
  • There is no need to delay breastfeeding until the infant is fully immunized. The risk of HBV mother-to-child transmission through breastfeeding is negligible if infants born to HIV-positive mothers receive the HBIG/HBV vaccine at birth.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 498

questions.stem: The pre-core mutants in hepatitis B are characterized by the notable absence of:
questions.solutionHtml:
HBeAg
  • A pre-core mutant is a variety of hepatitis B virus that does not produce hepatitis B virus e antigen (HBeAg).
  • These mutants are essential because infections caused by these viruses are difficult to treat and can cause infections of prolonged duration and with a higher risk of liver cirrhosis.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 499

questions.stem: Best term describing hepatitis B vaccine:
questions.solutionHtml:
Recombinant DNA vaccine
  • The hepatitis B vaccine is a safe and effective vaccine recommended for all infants at birth and children up to 18 years old.
  • The hepatitis B vaccine is also recommended for adults with diabetes and those at high risk for infection due to their jobs, lifestyle, living situations, or country of birth.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 499

questions.stem: You receive a phone call from a Dermatologist who is seeing a patient with porphyria cutanea tarda. The patient is found to have an elevated serum ALT. Which of the following tests would you recommend the Dermatologist to order?
questions.solutionHtml:
Anti-HCV
  • Porphyria cutanea tarda (PCT) is a type of porphyria or blood disorder that affects the skin. PCT is one of the most common types of porphyria.
  • It's sometimes referred to colloquially as vampire disease. That's because people with this condition often experience symptoms following exposure to sunlight.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 500

questions.stem: A 25-year-old male tests positive for a hepatitis C infection. Which of the following is the most likely method of transmission?
questions.solutionHtml:
Intravenous drug (needles)
  • Injection drug users (IDUs) are at risk of hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection due to needle and syringe sharing.
  • Chronic HCV infection is a major cause of liver-related morbidity and mortality but can be cured with antiviral treatment leading to sustained viral response (SVR).


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 500

questions.stem: Which of the following is a defective virus?
questions.solutionHtml:
Hepatitis D
  • Hepatitis D virus, also known as hepatitis delta virus, is a defective virus that is closely associated with HBV.
  • Although HDV can replicate autonomously, it requires the presence of HBV for virion assembly and secretion; thus, all patients with HDV are coinfected with HBV.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 500

questions.stem: HDV is a defective virus that requires its helper to provide:
questions.solutionHtml:
Reverse transcriptase
  • Hepatitis D virus, or hepatitis delta virus, is a defective virus closely associated with HBV.
  • Although HDV can replicate autonomously, it requires the presence of HBV for virion assembly and secretion; thus, all patients with HDV are coinfected with HBV.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 500

questions.stem: All true about hepatitis except:

options.label: A
options.text: HAV and HEV Hepatitis E Virus are transmitted feco-orally

options.label: B
options.text: An effective killed vaccine is available for HCV

options.label: C
options.text: HAV produces acute but not chronic hepatitis

options.label: D
options.text: HDV can only affect persons co-infected with hepatitis B.

questions.answerText: An effective killed vaccine is available for HCV
questions.solutionHtml:
An effective killed vaccine is available for HCV
  • A hepatitis C vaccine, capable of protecting against the hepatitis C virus (HCV), is not yet available.
  • Although vaccines exist for hepatitis A and hepatitis B, developing an HCV vaccine has presented challenges.
  • No vaccine is available, but several vaccines are under development.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 500

questions.stem: Most severe infections in HAV are seen in:
questions.solutionHtml:
Adults
  • Most adults with HAV Hepatitis A virus infection have a symptomatic illness that begins with abrupt onset of nausea, anorexia, fever, malaise, and abdominal pain.
  • Within a few days to a week, dark urine and acholic stools appear, followed by jaundice and pruritus.
  • Adults are more likely to have symptoms than children.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 501

questions.stem: Your patient developed clinical symptoms of hepatitis after visiting several Asian countries like Bangladesh and Myanmar. Likely cause:
questions.solutionHtml:
HEV Hepatitis E Virus
  • Hepatitis E is a liver disease caused by the infection known as hepatitis E virus (HEV).
  • Every year, there are an estimated 20 million HEV infections worldwide, leading to an estimated 3.3 million symptomatic cases of hepatitis E.
  • The virus has been mainly associated with the consumption of raw or undercooked pork meat or offal but also with wild boar meat, venison, and shellfish.
  • The study confirms that HEV infections occur throughout the year and is a major (34%) cause of acute jaundice in tertiary hospitals in Bangladesh.
  • Three-quarters of the acute hepatitis E cases were male, and HEV infection was higher among patients residing in urban areas than in rural areas.
  • HEV, previously called enterically transmitted non-A, non-B hepatitis, is a major cause of epidemic hepatitis and acute, sporadic hepatitis in developing countries.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 501
